![MLC-LLM for Jetson AGX Xavier](docs/_static/img/945-82972-0040-000.png)

This fork runs **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B** on **Jetson AGX Xavier 32 GB**
using JetPack 5 / CUDA 11.4. It adds DFlash speculative decoding and kernels
suited to Xavier's Volta GPU. The fastest measured configuration reaches
**395 tok/s prefill at 448 tokens**, **279 tok/s at 1,768 tokens**, and roughly
**31–34 tok/s decode**.

Based on upstream MLC-LLM `44fd06d0`. DFlash builds on
[Lev Stambler's implementation](https://github.com/Lev-Stambler/mlc-llm--DFlash/tree/b6c7bf7d269fd4127fd1a48c478b01d9dc8ff42b).
The original project overview is preserved in [README.upstream.md](README.upstream.md).

## Benchmarks: this fork versus baseline MLC

All results below run **Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B** on the same Xavier. Rates are
in tokens/second. Baseline uses upstream MLC with the CUDA 11.4 compatibility
fixes needed to run it, q4f16_1 weights and plain decoding. The optimized fork
uses the same target quantization, an F16 DFlash draft with two proposals,
Q8 activation kernels, and `--prefill-variant hybrid`.

| Prompt tokens | Baseline prefill | Fork prefill | Baseline decode | Fork decode | Fork decode MTP |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 161 | 108.28 | **240.79** | 11.90 | 23.24 | **31.68** |
| 448 | 115.47 | **395.16** | 10.80 | 19.63 | **34.16** |
| 1,768 | 82.66 | **278.67** | 10.06 | 17.18 | **31.10** |

**Fork decode** is the November 1 native-matrix, non-speculative control,
measured before the prefill changes (see the
[experiment record](docs/deploy/xavier_dflash.md)). **Fork decode MTP** uses
two-token DFlash speculative decoding with the final `hybrid` prefill configuration.

This compares the complete optimized configuration with the initial engine;
it includes speculative decoding and changed arithmetic. Baseline measurements
were recorded on October 31; fork measurements on November 1, 2026. The power
connection changed between sessions, and CPU compilation overlapped the initial
baseline. These are historical end-to-end engine comparisons. For an isolated
prefill comparison, the following November 1 sweep keeps the weights, compiled
model library, DFlash settings and machine configuration identical:

| Prefill implementation | 161 tokens | 448 tokens | 1,768 tokens | Long first token |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fork before prefill changes | 218.91 | 271.75 | 143.94 | 12.292 s |
| Skip fully masked tiles | 235.07 | 345.13 | 201.56 | 8.781 s |
| + Actual-width local heads (`width`) | 233.16 | 340.26 | 250.50 | 7.068 s |
| + Volta WMMA for current-chunk attention (`hybrid`) | **240.79** | **395.16** | **278.67** | **6.354 s** |

The combined prefill changes improve the long prompt **1.94×** and cut its
complete 128-token request from **16.354 to 10.438 seconds**. Decode stays
approximately constant. The `width` variant preserves all six measured baseline
output strings; `hybrid` changes the long forced continuation.

## Benchmarks: this fork versus llama.cpp

Both engines run **Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B with two DFlash proposals**, the same
prompt text and a forced 128-token output. MLC uses q4f16_1 plus Q8 activations;
llama.cpp uses Q4_K_M and the F16 draft, with CUDA offload and Flash Attention.
The tokenizer/template counts differ slightly.

| Prompt tokens MLC / llama | Fork prefill | llama prefill | Fork decode | llama decode | Fork request | llama request |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 161 / 168 | **240.79** | 189.90 | **31.68** | 26.80 | **4.681 s** | 5.635 s |
| 448 / 454 | **395.16** | 316.46 | **34.16** | 25.09 | **4.856 s** | 6.511 s |
| 1,768 / 1,774 | 278.67 | **341.88** | **31.10** | 24.37 | 10.438 s | 10.427 s |

The fork is faster on short and medium complete requests. Llama prefills the
long input faster; the complete long request is effectively tied. The llama
control was recorded earlier on November 1 at revision `ddf48f85`, before the
final MLC prefill sweep. Different quantizations and arithmetic mean this is a
practical serving comparison, with no claim of equal model accuracy.

**Method:** AGX Xavier 32 GB, sm_72, MAXN, pinned clocks (GPU 1,377 MHz, CPU
2,265.6 MHz, EMC 2,133 MHz), one sequence, context 8,192, MLC chunks 512,
prefix caching disabled, greedy generation, one warmup and two measured runs
per case. Tables report means; profiler timings are excluded. Forced output
past EOS measures throughput rather than natural answer quality. Raw summaries
are in [docs/benchmarks/xavier](docs/benchmarks/xavier); detailed validation and
history are in [the experiment record](docs/deploy/xavier_dflash.md).

## Additional model: Gemma4 Unified 12B

An experimental port of the official `Gemma4UnifiedAssistantForCausalLM` also
supports native MTP trials with this target. See the
[MTP implementation, validation and build instructions](docs/deploy/xavier_gemma4_mtp.md).
It currently uses a greedy direct-VM controller with a 4K deployed context and native tool calls.
The optional HTTP adapter keeps it resident alongside Nemotron and routes
requests by model ID through one shared GPU queue.

The fork also supports text generation from
`gemma-4-12B-IT-QAT-Q4_0-unquantized-heretic`, converted from BF16 to MLC
`q4f16_1` (6.70 GB of tensors). These are **plain-decoding** results on the
same Xavier, with a 4K context, chunks of 512, one warmup and two measured
128-token runs per prompt:

| Prompt tokens | Prefill tok/s | Decode tok/s | Complete request |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 161 | 90.82 | 11.72 | 12.616 s |
| 448 | 109.65 | 10.59 | 16.082 s |
| 1,768 | 50.44 | 8.73 | 49.607 s |

This first port uses the fast projection kernels and generic attention;
the Nemotron-specific attention optimizations do not apply to its different
head layout. See [the 12B experiment](docs/deploy/xavier_gemma4_12b.md) for
conversion/build instructions, validation and native-MTP compatibility, and
[the saved summary](docs/benchmarks/xavier/gemma4-12b-heretic-summary.json)
for the measured means.

The experimental z-lab DFlash pairing did not accelerate this checkpoint:
**6.84 versus 11.72 tok/s** on the short prompt, with **zero accepted draft
tokens**. The 12B experiment records the input-scaling correction and remaining
compatibility investigation; these plain rates do not include speculative decoding.

## Improvements in this fork

- **CUDA 11.4 support:** pinned TVM/TIRx compatibility patches, nvcc instead of
  the newer NVRTC bindings, and a fix for exporting shared module graphs.
- **Gemma4 support:** E4B/Nemotron with two KV heads, plus a text-only Unified
  12B port with mixed local/global KV head counts and global K=V projections.
- **Native Unified MTP prototype:** official QAT assistant conversion, shared-KV
  draft steps, greedy target verification, and an optional resident HTTP adapter.
- **Resident model routing:** Nemotron shares one authenticated endpoint and
  FIFO GPU queue with either 12B + MTP or EmbeddingGemma 2 text embeddings;
  see the [resident switching PoC](docs/deploy/xavier_embedding_switch_poc.md).
- **Faster projections:** one-token GEMV specialization; FP16 dequantization +
  cuBLAS for large prefill; native DP4A/Q8-activation kernels for 1–4 rows.
- **DFlash execution:** target feature extraction, GPU greedy selection, cached
  draft K/V, bounded context attention, FP32 residual fixes and CUDA graphs.
- **Faster attention:** native 256/512-wide verification; prefill skips masked
  tiles, computes local paged heads at width 256, and optionally uses Volta
  Tensor Cores for current-chunk attention.
- **Reproducible experiments:** fixed prompts, component tests, monitored runners
  and separate prefill variants.
- **Xavier HTTPS service:** authenticated OpenAI-compatible chat and native
  Nemotron/Gemma4 tool round-trips for Pi; see the
  [deployment runbook](deploy/xavier/README.md).

## Build on Jetson AGX Xavier

### 1. System and Python environment

Tested with **JetPack 5.1.8 / L4T R35.7.0, Ubuntu 20.04, CUDA 11.4,
gcc 9.4, Python 3.12, LLVM 20.1.8 and CMake 4.4.4**. Install LLVM 20 development
packages using the [LLVM apt repository](https://apt.llvm.org/), plus a recent
Rust toolchain for the tokenizer build. Keep `/usr/local/cuda` pointed at CUDA
11.4. The system Python 3.8 is too old for this source tree.

```bash
sudo apt-get install build-essential git ccache pkg-config libssl-dev bc llvm-20-dev
# Install uv first: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/
mkdir -p ~/Workspaces
cd ~/Workspaces
git clone --recursive https://github.com/cortexist/mlc-llm.git
cd mlc-llm
uv venv --python 3.12 --seed ~/Workspaces/mlc-venv
source scripts/xavier/env.sh
uv pip install 'cmake==4.4.4' ninja 'scikit-build-core>=0.11,!=1.1.0' \
  setuptools-scm 'cython>=3.2.8' numpy ml_dtypes packaging psutil \
  datasets fastapi openai pandas prompt_toolkit requests safetensors \
  sentencepiece shortuuid tiktoken tqdm transformers uvicorn
uv pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
uv pip install --no-deps apache-tvm-ffi-orcjit==0.1.3
```

CPU PyTorch is sufficient for the conversion/validation helpers. The tested
packages were torch `2.15.0+cpu`, transformers `5.22.1` and numpy `2.5.4`.
FlashInfer starts at SM75; Xavier is SM72, so this build uses its own attention
paths. The optional source-built orcjit addon requires a newer LLVM; the tested
setup used the prebuilt 0.1.3 package above.

### 2. Build the pinned compiler stack and runtime

The recursive checkout pins TVM `629cc65820`, TIRx `198a04573e` and TVM-FFI
`6628c464e3`. Apply the included dependency patch **before building**:

```bash
source scripts/xavier/env.sh
git -C "$TIRX_SRC" apply --check "$MLC_SRC/scripts/xavier/patches/tirx-cuda114.patch"
git -C "$TIRX_SRC" apply "$MLC_SRC/scripts/xavier/patches/tirx-cuda114.patch"
bash scripts/xavier/build-all.sh
```

Apply the patch once per clean dependency checkout. It includes the CUDA launch
compatibility definitions, nvcc default and export-order fix. Build order is
FFI → TIRx → TVM → MLC. The scripts enable CUDA and cuBLAS, disable
Thrust/CUTLASS/NVTX, target architecture 72, and link pthread explicitly for
Ubuntu 20.04. Compilation defaults to two jobs. Installing all four from the
same pinned source avoids FFI ABI mismatches.

### 3. Prepare Nemotron and the DFlash draft

Place the BF16 Hugging Face checkpoint
[`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16)
in `~/Models/nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16`, and its matching DFlash F16 GGUF at
`~/Models/nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-4GB/Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-DFlash-F16.gguf`.
The tested draft uses block size 8, mask token 4 and target layers
`[5, 11, 17, 23, 35]` (zero-based). Keep a llama.cpp checkout at
`~/Workspaces/llama.cpp` for `gguf-py` and the comparison server.

```bash
source scripts/xavier/env.sh
export MLC_GEMMA4_TEXT_ONLY=1
mkdir -p dist/nemotron-q4 dist/libs logs
python -m mlc_llm convert_weight ~/Models/nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16 \
  --quantization q4f16_1 --device cuda -o dist/nemotron-q4
python -m mlc_llm gen_config ~/Models/nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16 \
  --quantization q4f16_1 --conv-template gemma4_instruction \
  --context-window-size 8192 --prefill-chunk-size 512 --max-batch-size 1 \
  -o dist/nemotron-q4
python scripts/prepare_xavier_dflash.py --target dist/nemotron-q4 \
  --draft ~/Models/nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-4GB/Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-DFlash-F16.gguf
python -m mlc_llm convert_weight dist/draft-hf --quantization q0f16 \
  --model-type dflash --device cpu -o dist/draft
export MLC_DFLASH_CUDA_GRAPH=1 MLC_JP5_SINGLE_TOKEN=1 MLC_JP5_VERIFY_THREE=1
export MLC_JP5_Q4_CUBLAS=1
# The draft's Tensor Core compilation path uses its model-specific override.
env -u MLC_JP5_Q4_CUBLAS python -m mlc_llm compile dist/draft/mlc-chat-config.json \
  --device cuda --opt O2 -o dist/libs/draft-cached-tc-sm72.so
bash scripts/build_xavier_kernels.sh
python scripts/build_xavier_prefill.py
```

`prepare_xavier_dflash.py` exports the F16/F32 draft tensors without
requantization and reuses the converted target via local symlinks. It also
accepts `--gguf-python` for a different `gguf-py` location. Keep the original
converted target directory available. `MLC_GEMMA4_TEXT_ONLY=1` omits audio entry
points that do not compile on this target. Only text generation was qualified.

### 4. Validate and reproduce the benchmark

```bash
source scripts/xavier/env.sh
sudo nvpmodel -m 0
sudo jetson_clocks
python tests/python/op/test_xavier_prefill.py --output logs/prefill-components.json
bash scripts/run_xavier_prefill_experiments.sh
# Individual optimized run:
python scripts/bench_xavier_dflash.py --prefill-variant hybrid \
  --target-lib dist/libs/target-dflash-dp4a-attn-sm72.so --draft-tokens 2 \
  --output logs/nemotron-hybrid.json
# llama.cpp control; uses ~/Workspaces/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server:
python scripts/bench_xavier_llama.py --output logs/llama-control.json
```

`width` is the simpler prefill choice; `hybrid` additionally uses FP16
probabilities in WMMA attention. Both preserve the existing small-query
verification path. **108 component checks** passed, including independent
FP32 attention comparisons and three-query fallback checks. Elevated Compute
Sanitizer memcheck completed with **zero errors**. Natural-stop tests returned
`391`, the requested three summary bullets plus two risks, and `Done`.

The tested configuration is greedy, one sequence, two draft proposals, prefix
caching disabled and an 8K context. Q8 activations and WMMA change arithmetic;
broad accuracy/perplexity equivalence has not been established. Board shutdowns
also occurred during the investigation; these measurements do not establish
long-term hardware stability. Benchmark runners use temperature/memory stop
limits. Keep compilation and GPU inference sequential.

## HTTPS serving on Xavier

The optional service exposes an OpenAI-compatible API on the LAN or a
Headscale/Tailscale network. Use your own hostname, such as
`https://xavier.example.com/v1`. It supports resident Nemotron with either
the 12B/MTP adapter or the EmbeddingGemma 2 text worker. It uses a
certificate signed by a local CA, bearer authentication and streaming responses.
Requests share one GPU queue; the 12B adapter supports 4K text/tool chat, and
the embedding PoC accepts up to 128 text tokens.
See the
[deployment and client instructions](deploy/xavier/README.md) for CA trust,
credentials, service management and certificate renewal.

## Upstream and attribution

[MLC-LLM](https://github.com/mlc-ai/mlc-llm) and its contributors provide the
compiler and serving engine. DFlash was ported from Lev Stambler's fork; its
history and source attribution are retained. This repository retains the
upstream [Apache-2.0 license](LICENSE). See [README.upstream.md](README.upstream.md)
for the broader upstream project, documentation and contribution links.

# Resident model HTTPS service on Xavier

Hostnames, addresses and machine-specific paths below are examples. Replace
`xavier.example.com`, `192.0.2.10`, the tailnet address and SSH aliases with your
own values. Historical network identifiers are anonymized in public summaries;
benchmark measurements are unchanged.

The optional **embedding switching PoC** profile is currently active: resident
`nemotron` chat and `embeddinggemma-2` text embeddings share the same GPU queue.
The 12B worker is unloaded by `embedding-poc.conf`; its artifacts and the base
dual-chat configuration below are retained. See the
[PoC measurements, API and restore instructions](../../docs/deploy/xavier_embedding_switch_poc.md).

The deployed OpenAI-compatible API is **`https://xavier.example.com/v1`**, with
model IDs **`nemotron`** and **`gemma4-12b`**. `/healthz` reports readiness. Model listing and
generation require `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`.

Both targets and their assistants stay resident. Select the model in each
chat request; switching does not unload/reload weights. One shared FIFO queue
serializes complete generations across both models, including streaming and
Nemotron tool calls. `X-Xavier-Queue-Wait-Ms` reports time spent waiting.
The existing Pi default remains Nemotron.
The existing `nemotron:e4b` client ID is also accepted as a Nemotron alias.

| API model | Decoder | Context | Tools | Response streaming |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `nemotron` | DFlash | 16,384 | Yes | Incremental chat; buffered tool turns |
| `gemma4-12b` | Official QAT MTP, two proposals | 4,096 | Yes | Buffered SSE with keepalives |

The 12B route uses the Heretic target and the original Unified QAT assistant.
It supports text `/v1/chat/completions`, greedy single-output generation,
and native Gemma4 tool calls, and reserves two context slots for verification. `max_tokens` must fit the
remaining context; its default is the smaller of 512 or the available budget.
Oversized inputs and forced tool choices, stop strings, penalties, logprobs,
response constraints and debug settings return HTTP 400. Unknown model IDs
return HTTP 404. This HTTP adapter uses the direct-VM implementation;
it does not add an `MLCEngine` MTP speculative mode. See
[the MTP build and validation notes](../../docs/deploy/xavier_gemma4_mtp.md).

## Access from clients

- On the LAN, the router resolves `xavier.example.com` to `192.0.2.10`.
- On the existing Headscale tailnet, MagicDNS's extra record resolves the same
  name to `100.64.0.10`. Enable Tailscale DNS on the client. Xavier itself
  retains LAN DNS with `--accept-dns=false`.
- Clients must trust their local CA certificate, or pass that file as their CA
  bundle. Ensure the CA's name constraints permit your chosen hostname and
  the leaf certificate includes it. Use the same hostname over the tailnet.
- The API key is stored with mode 0600 at
  `benchmark-client:~/.config/xavier/api-key` and
  `xavier:~/.config/mlc-nemotron/api-key`. Copy it securely to authorized
  clients; keep it out of source control.

On a client with the root certificate and key file copied locally:

```bash
export XAVIER_API_KEY="$(cat ~/.config/xavier/api-key)"
curl --cacert ./local-ca.crt https://xavier.example.com/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $XAVIER_API_KEY"
curl -N --cacert ./local-ca.crt https://xavier.example.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $XAVIER_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"nemotron","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello."}],"max_tokens":128,"stream":true}'
```

For an SDK or application, set its base URL to `https://xavier.example.com/v1`,
its model to `nemotron` or `gemma4-12b`, and its API key to the saved key. Configure its TLS
trust store with the local CA. An explicit tailnet connectivity test can use
`curl --resolve xavier.example.com:443:100.64.0.10` with the same CA and credentials.

## Installed services

`mlc-nemotron.service` runs as `zero` from the validated experimental checkout
at `/home/zero/Workspaces/mlc-dflash-work`. It uses that checkout's Python
code, runtime, converted weights and compiled model libraries. The API listens
on `127.0.0.1:8000`. Nginx terminates TLS on port 443, permits LAN/loopback and
tailnet clients, and passes streaming responses without buffering. Public IPv6
clients are denied. No router port forwarding or Tailscale Funnel is configured.

The model configuration is the measured Nemotron target, F16 DFlash draft,
two proposals (`spec_draft_length=3`), `hybrid` prefill, one active sequence,
16K context and prefix caching disabled. Multiple HTTP clients can queue
requests. The service restarts on failure, with a bounded restart rate.
Nginx, MLC and tailscaled are enabled at boot.

`mlc-nemotron.service.d/dual-model.conf` sets `MLC_GEMMA4_MTP=1`, enabling the
second resident target/assistant and an arithmetic startup check. The API
becomes ready after both models load. Startup loads and warms 12B first, then
initializes Nemotron: a Nemotron-first restart encountered a late 1 GiB NvMap
allocation failure despite available system RAM. The MTP VM is constructed and called on
one dedicated thread; cancellation drains that worker before releasing the
shared GPU queue. Its chat template comes from the original Heretic checkpoint,
because MLC conversion omits `chat_template.jinja`.

To install the optional second model after building the MTP artifacts, copy
`scripts/gemma4_mtp_service.py`, `scripts/bench_xavier_mtp.py`,
`scripts/xavier_serve_queue.py` and the updated `scripts/serve_xavier_nemotron.py`
to the deployed checkout, then install the drop-in:

```bash
sudo install -d /etc/systemd/system/mlc-nemotron.service.d
sudo install -m 644 deploy/xavier/dual-model.conf \
  /etc/systemd/system/mlc-nemotron.service.d/dual-model.conf
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart mlc-nemotron
```

For Nemotron-only operation, set `Environment=MLC_GEMMA4_MTP=0` in that drop-in,
reload systemd and restart the service. Keep the shared-queue helper beside the
serving script in either mode. No nginx, certificate, DNS or API-key change is
needed when enabling/disabling the second model.

Generation defaults to `temperature: 0`. Explicit nonzero temperatures or
`n` values other than 1 return HTTP 400: the experimental Xavier DFlash
sampler is qualified for greedy, single-output requests. Non-greedy sampling
can otherwise terminate its background worker.

### Pi on benchmark-client

`~/.pi/agent/models.json` registers `xavier/nemotron:e4b`, reads the API key
from the private credential file, and declares the 16384-token context and
2048-token output limit. `~/.pi/agent/bin/pi-xavier` selects it and loads
the system trust store through `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` before Node starts:

```bash
pi-xavier
# Or select the provider directly:
NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 \
  pi --provider xavier --model nemotron:e4b --thinking off
```

On benchmark-client, the root is installed at
`/etc/ca-certificates/trust-source/anchors/local-ca.crt` and extracted by
`sudo update-ca-trust`. `/etc/environment` and
`/etc/profile.d/local-node-system-ca.sh` enable Node system-store trust for new
login sessions. Existing shells can run `export NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1`. Some
applications maintain independent trust stores and need their own configuration.

Pi uses `openai-completions`, bearer authentication, `max_tokens`, system-role
messages and greedy sampling. Its per-model compaction settings reserve 2048
tokens and keep 4096 recent tokens. The default provider is `xavier` and the default client model is
`nemotron:e4b`. The `pi-llama-cpp` package remains installed with
`extensions: []`, suppressing its independent localhost:9931 startup probe;
re-enable it through `pi config` when using that integration. The ordinary Pi
launcher defaults `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` for existing terminal environments.
Tools are enabled: the launcher has no `--no-tools` flag and the model's
`samplingParams` contains `temperature: 0, top_p: 1` without `tool_choice: none`.
Start a new Pi process after changing its model configuration.

`models.json` also registers `xavier/gemma4-12b` (4,096 context, 512 output
tokens), with compaction reserve/retention of 768/1024. Reopen `/model` to reload
Pi's local registry. Nemotron remains the default. For a fresh 12B session on benchmark-client:

```bash
~/.pi/agent/bin/pi-gemma4
```

The launcher enables read/bash/edit/write with a short system prompt and omits
MCP, extensions, skills and workspace context files to fit the smaller window.
Long existing coding transcripts may still exceed 4K. Both models accept native
OpenAI tool-call histories and text content blocks. Tools execute on the client.
12B buffers tool calls before emitting complete OpenAI SSE deltas.

Pi 1.4.0's fixed 4,096-token safety margin clamps a 4K model's output to one
token, so the 12B model sets `samplingParams.max_tokens: 512` explicitly. Server
checks still enforce the actual prompt/output/verification budget.

`pi-clm` also remains installed with `extensions: []`. Its default guard uses
`window − 4096 − reserve` (2048 input tokens on this model), so it withheld even
a one-line read result and then withheld the model's attempt to retrieve it.
Pi's own configured compaction remains active. Re-enable the extension through
`pi config` when using a suitable context size or after tuning its policy.

### Native Gemma4 tool calling

The Xavier serving script installs `scripts/gemma4_tools.py` ahead of MLC's
ordinary chat route. Requests with tools or tool history use the Nemotron
checkpoint's NVIDIA chat template, including native tool declarations, calls
and results. Raw completion generation uses the same optimized engine and
DFlash configuration. A parser converts complete native calls to OpenAI
`tool_calls` with JSON argument strings, and accepts the corresponding
`role: tool` results on subsequent requests. Pi executes tools on the client
computer; the service only generates calls.

The adapter loads tokenizer/template files from
`~/Models/nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16`, or `MLC_NEMOTRON_TOKENIZER` when set.
It does not load that checkpoint's BF16 weights. Keep its tokenizer files and
`chat_template.jinja`; this deployment uses Transformers 5.22.1 from the
existing MLC virtual environment. Copy the adapter beside the serving script
when deploying, along with the protocol update accepting string arguments.

Supported tool choices are `auto` (the default) and `none`; forced/required
tool choices, tool-conversation images, logprobs and response-format constraints
are not implemented. Tool generations are buffered until the turn completes,
then emitted as OpenAI SSE deltas with usage and finish reasons. SSE comments
keep the connection active during generation. Malformed/incomplete calls and
undeclared tool names produce errors rather than executable partial calls.
Ordinary chat without tools retains MLC's existing streaming path. The model context limits and greedy-only restriction still apply.

CPU regression checks:

```bash
python tests/python/serve/test_gemma4_tools.py
# In the deployed MLC environment, this also exercises typed requests and SSE:
PYTHONPATH=python MLC_LIBRARY_PATH=build \
  ~/Workspaces/mlc-venv/bin/python tests/python/serve/test_gemma4_tools.py
```

Verified over HTTPS: a native `read` request returned a structured tool call;
the next streaming turn accepted its matching result and quoted its proof word.
All seven CPU checks pass in the deployed environment. A real Pi run with the
ordinary tools and workspace context read a local file and returned its exact
random proof word. No file contents were included in the user's test prompt.

```bash
ssh xavier 'sudo systemctl status mlc-nemotron nginx tailscaled'
ssh xavier 'sudo journalctl -u mlc-nemotron -f'
```

# Gemma4 Unified 12B on Xavier

The official QAT assistant now has a separate
[native MTP prototype and short measured trial](xavier_gemma4_mtp.md), using
`Gemma4UnifiedAssistantForCausalLM`. It accepts proposals with this target;
the DFlash experiment below remains a separate, unsuccessful pairing.

The additional `gemma4_unified` model entry supports text generation from
`~/Models/gemma-4-12B-IT-QAT-Q4_0-unquantized-heretic` on xavier. Its source
contains 11,907,350,320 text parameters in BF16; the small audio and vision
components are excluded. MLC converts these values to `q4f16_1`. The source's
`Q4_0-unquantized` name describes its QAT lineage, not its on-disk tensor dtype.

This dense architecture differs from the E-series model used by Nemotron:
48 layers, hidden size 3840, 16 query heads, eight local KV heads and one global

eight cache slots. It also pads local head dimensions from 256 to 512, as the
E-series implementation does. Both choices preserve the attention calculation
but cost memory and attention work. The Nemotron-specific attention/prefill
callbacks are not enabled for this model. Small-batch Q8/DP4A projections and
cuBLAS prefill projections are enabled in the measured library.

## Implementation and limits

- The four-layer assistant uses its own tied embedding/LM-head weights,
  pre/post projections, and the target's last local/global KV states. It has
  query/output projections, without independent K/V projections.
- Each draft step concatenates the scaled target embedding and previous hidden
  state. Shared KV and position stay fixed within a draft round; the assistant's
  projected hidden state feeds its next step. This follows the installed
  Transformers 5.22.1 candidate generator and
  [Unified assistant implementation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/gemma4_unified_assistant).
- New target exports return normalized hidden states and unpadded, unbroadcast
  KV deltas. Verification accepts the greedy matching prefix and rolls back
  rejected target-cache entries. The controller retains only committed deltas.
  Prompt prefill uses chunks of at most 512, preserving shared KV between chunks.
- One sequence, greedy generation, one or two proposals, 4,096 total tokens.
  Local assistant layers mask older shared KV using the reference sliding-window
  rule; global layers retain the complete valid history.
- Assistant KV inputs are padded to the compiled capacity (4,096 in deployment) and masked by valid length. Explicit
  attention reductions avoid CUDA 11.4 cuBLAS-Lt strided-batch dispatch errors;
  fixed buffers avoid a dynamic stack allocation limitation in CUDA codegen.
- The Python controller copies KV, hidden states, logits and embeddings through
  CPU memory. Reported times include this overhead. Persistent GPU buffers,
  cache views, device sampling and native engine integration remain future work.

## What was implemented

This is the actual local `~/Models/embeddinggemma-2` text checkpoint: 271,002,648
parameters, extracted without modifying the original multimodal checkpoint.
MLC converts them to FP32 (`q0f32`, 1,084,010,592 tensor bytes), with no additional
quantization. Xavier has no native BF16; the
[model card](https://huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-2) explicitly warns
against FP16. Vision/audio and d1-Omni are outside this first PoC.

The implementation includes bidirectional grouped-query attention, separate
local/global head layouts, Q/K/V normalization, RoPE, projection-only per-layer
inputs, layer scalars and the trained 512→768 projection. An entire small encoder
matches Transformers on CPU, including masked padding and a small sliding
window, with maximum errors below `2e-7`. FP16 conversion is explicitly rejected.

The GPU worker uses one fixed, padded 128-token bucket and processes batch items
sequentially. It adds the checkpoint's BOS and EOS explicitly: MLC's tokenizer
encodes content without Hugging Face post-processing. Valid tokens are
mean-pooled and L2-normalized. Longer inputs fail with HTTP 400; nothing is
silently truncated. The native checkpoint's advertised 8K context is not
implemented by this bounded PoC.

Four real-checkpoint vectors were compared against Transformers 5.22.1 CPU
FP32. Token counts match (64 total); maximum vector error was `2.51e-7`, with
all cosine similarities above `0.999999999997`. Query/relevant-document cosine
was 0.899829, versus 0.543209 for the unrelated document. These are functional
checks, not a retrieval-quality evaluation.

## Switching measurements

November 1, 2026; Xavier AGX 32GB, JetPack 5.1.8, CUDA 11.4, fixed MAXN clocks,
cool fan profile. One persistent HTTPS connection from benchmark-client, matched inputs,
two warmups per model, 16 samples per model/mode. Repeated-model blocks and
alternating pairs run in both orders. Prefix caching is disabled. The Nemotron
prompt asks for 17×23, with a 16-token output limit; every response is `391`.
The embedding input is the same short password-reset search query on every call.

| Median latency | Repeated same model | Alternating models | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Nemotron complete HTTPS response | 530.19 ms | 525.95 ms | −4.24 ms |
| Embedding complete HTTPS response | 55.40 ms | 56.12 ms | +0.71 ms |
| Embedding compiled forward + output copy | 42.13 ms | 41.40 ms | −0.73 ms |

The embedding forward timer synchronizes before the VM call and stops after
copying the per-token output to CPU. It excludes tokenization/input copies,
pooling, JSON serialization and networking; it is not a CUDA-event kernel-only
timer. The worker median including preprocessing/pooling was 43.91 / 43.17 ms.
The HTTPS embedding P10–P90 ranges were 54.20–59.11 ms repeated and
55.48–57.87 ms alternating. Both workers remained resident in the same PID
(1942), and the embedding instance ID stayed unchanged across all calls.

This experiment found no material alternating-request penalty. The small signed
differences overlap ordinary request variation; they are **not an isolated CUDA
context-switch measurement**, a p99 SLA, or evidence of zero hardware overhead.
It does demonstrate that switching needs no checkpoint reload or per-request
weight transfer. Full raw timings and verification are saved in
[the result summary](../benchmarks/xavier/embedding-switch-poc-summary.json).

The existing queue still serializes whole requests. In a concurrent check, a
short embedding waited 1,619 ms for the active Nemotron generation, then took
41.60 ms for its forward/copy. Token/block preemption and priority scheduling
have not been implemented. Resident weights remove loading delays; they do not
remove contention for GPU time.

## API

Use the existing CA trust and bearer key. No TLS/DNS/port change is needed.

```bash
curl https://xavier.example.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $XAVIER_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embeddinggemma-2","input":"task: search result | query: how do I reset my password?"}'
```

Inputs are one string or 1–16 strings. Task prefixes are supplied by the caller;
the service does not choose a retrieval task silently. Documents can use
`title: none | text: ...`. The endpoint supports `dimensions` 128/256/512/768,
renormalizes after truncation, and returns floats or `encoding_format: base64`.
Headers report worker/forward time, queue wait and the resident embedding
instance ID. Input/normalization checks, base64 output and overlong rejection
were exercised over HTTPS.

## Build, reproduce and restore

With the Xavier toolchain from the main deployment instructions:

```bash
sudo systemctl stop mlc-nemotron
bash scripts/build_xavier_embedding_poc.sh
# Copy the new model registry/module and service helpers to the deployed checkout
# when building somewhere other than the active source tree.
sudo install -m 644 deploy/xavier/embedding-poc.conf \
  /etc/systemd/system/mlc-nemotron.service.d/embedding-poc.conf
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl start mlc-nemotron
```

The build produces `dist/embeddinggemma2-text-q0f32` and
`dist/libs/embeddinggemma2-text-f32-s128-sm72.so`. It needs no new C++ runtime
build. Keep compilation and inference separate. The new serving script needs
`embeddinggemma2_service.py` and `bench_xavier_mtp.py` beside it. The embedding
VM is initialized and used on its own single thread; cancellation drains GPU
work before releasing the same queue used by chat/tool requests.

```bash
python scripts/bench_xavier_switch.py --endpoint https://xavier.example.com \
  --key-file ~/.config/xavier/api-key --repeats 8 --output /tmp/switch.json
python tests/python/model/test_embeddinggemma2.py
python tests/python/serve/test_xavier_model_queue.py
```

For reference vectors, run `scripts/check_embeddinggemma2_reference.py` against
the original checkpoint on CPU. Local experimental records are under
`benchmark-client:~/Workspaces/xavier-llm-bench/mlc-jp5/logs/embedding-switch-poc-20261101`
and the corresponding remote `mlc-dflash-work/logs` directory.

To restore Nemotron + 12B, move the optional `embedding-poc.conf` drop-in out of
`/etc/systemd/system/mlc-nemotron.service.d`, reload systemd and restart the unit.
The retained `dual-model.conf` enables 12B again. The power/stability issue
remains deferred; this PoC uses only short requests and is not an uptime test.
